title: Helping Wiley sell his records door to door
summary: Williams helped Wiley sell his 1928 Brunswick records at houses and in bootleg places, playing piano to sell them.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: 19 and... 19 and 28. I don't know with what company, but he made that tune. Because he was around here selling them himself. And I helped him sell some of them. You know, at that time, 28 they had the old hand big trollers, you know. You can go to people's house and sell them. Yeah. He was selling them himself. Plugging them himself. I don't know what company he was on. I'm not going back to 35th and State no more. He made that tune.
Oh, I got it here. You'd better not go to 35th and State no more. Yeah. You see, I'm not going to tell you.
I helped him to sell them records. Yeah? Yeah. He's selling them to houses. We go in the house and play, and he sells the records. They had the old hand big trollers then, you know.
Yeah. And you can remember when he arrived here. You were here before he came. Yeah. I know when he came.
He had to have a boy come with him too. Come behind and could play too. Oh, wow. A little bit of thin, he talks thin like a wind. Yeah. Yeah. I don't know why.
You know, he recorded the first time June. Boy, he could play. He recorded the first time in summer 1926. And then you must have been come to Chicago before summer 1926. Uh-huh. This is good.

He might have come here on the record and they didn't stay, but he come here and stay in 19... Oh, yeah. I know when he come here to stay. Yeah. He was in the Angels building, Billy Smith and Warbats.

No, I don't think you're lying, no. But you have a terrific memory. Yeah. Yeah. I happened to sell those records. He used to bring them around his own, going to the house, to the house and sell them.
